title: Credential split by a backslash followed by CRLF
summary: A SendGrid-shaped key in an unquoted shell assignment is broken by a backslash followed by a carriage return and a line feed, as a script saved with Windows line endings would hold.
rationale: The cited shell texts define the continuation as a backslash followed by a newline. They do not say what a carriage return between them does, so whether this input is rebuilt, or the carriage return becomes part of the value, depends on how the shell reads the file. This is the line-ending variant of the shell continuation Case and is not assumed to behave the same.

expectation.rationale: Unresolved. POSIX and the Bash manual describe backslash followed by newline only; neither text states the carriage-return case. Candidate outcomes: reconstructed (must-flag, all fragments) or separator inserted. Reading the shell grammar or running a shell on the input would settle it. No assertable fixture. Synthetic, never issued: every value in the fixtures is built from the words SYNTHETIC and EXAMPLE, so none can authenticate.

sources.supports: If a newline follows the backslash, the shell shall interpret this as line continuation.
If a backslash-newline pair appears and the backslash is not quoted, the pair is treated as a line continuation.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
